metadata.title: LP47 First Principles R3: Protection Horizon Universality, Experimental Protocol, QEC Implications
metadata.author: B博士
metadata.polaris: 质量是因果环锁住信息的宏观表现
key_discoveries: Protection horizon is UNIVERSAL across graph topologies — NOT unique to rings
Cycle space dimension H_1(G) is NEITHER necessary NOR sufficient for protection
Star graph (beta_1=0) shows HIGHEST protection fraction (83-100%), refuting cycle-dependence hypothesis
Protection criterion revised to GRAPH-THEORETIC SHIELDING: perturbation at q is invisible when q lies in the 'graph shadow' of the measurement set
Double-ring (beta_1=2) DESTROYS q=0 protection present in standard ring — extra edge creates alternative path breaking symmetry cancellation
Experimental witness protocol designed: 6-qubit circuits, classical shadows, 10^5 shots, tomography-free QCMI measurement
QEC interpretation: protected positions are 'magic-blind zones' — errors invisible to specific QCMI probes, with MBQC implications

deliverable_1_universality.summary: Protection horizon tested on 5 graph types at n=6 with Hmix perturbation at each qubit q, measuring QCMI for partitions k=1,2,3 (A={0}, B={k}, C={k+1}). The core hypothesis that H_1(G) ≠ 0 is required for protection is REFUTED. Protection exists in acyclic graphs (star: beta_1=0, linear: beta_1=0) with protection fractions comparable to or exceeding the ring case.

hypothesis_test.original_hypothesis: Protection horizon requires non-trivial cycle space H_1(G) ≠ 0. 1D cycle space → protection depth δ. Higher-dimensional cycle space → multiple protection layers.
hypothesis_test.test_result: REFUTED. Star graph (H_1=0) shows 83-100% protection. Linear chain (H_1=0) shows 33-67% protection. The cycle space dimension does not correlate with protection fraction.
hypothesis_test.revised_hypothesis: Protection horizon is a GRAPH-THEORETIC SHIELDING phenomenon. A qubit q is protected for partition (A,B,C) when: (1) q is in the measurement set {A,B,C} AND the perturbation's effect is symmetrically cancelled by the stabilizer structure, OR (2) q is outside the measurement set but graph-theoretically 'shadowed' — its influence on the measurement set cancels due to symmetric alternative paths or graph automorphisms that preserve the measurement set.

cluster_ring.verification: MATCHES fp_r2 EXACTLY — R2 baseline reproduced

linear_cluster.analysis: End-qubits (0,1) are universally protected. Protection extends 2-3 qubits from A along the chain. q=5 protected for k=3 due to symmetry (end-of-chain mirror). No periodic boundary → no 'far side' activation pattern — instead, protection decays with distance from measurement set.

double_ring.critical_finding: q=0 PROTECTION DESTROYED by extra CZ(0,3) edge. In standard ring, q=0 is protected for k=1 (Δ=0). In double-ring, q=0 becomes ACTIVE (Δ=0.0347). Mechanism: CZ(0,3) creates alternative path 0→3→...→{1,2}, breaking the reflection symmetry that cancelled q=0's perturbation effect. This is the SMOKING GUN for the graph-shielding mechanism: adding a single edge that creates an alternative path to the measurement set can destroy protection.

star_graph.analysis: HIGHEST protection fraction (100% any-k). Center (q=0) protected for all k — star center's perturbation affects all leaves equally, and since the measurement involves only specific leaves, the symmetric effect cancels. The single active qubit for each k is always the 'C' qubit of the NEXT partition (k→k+1 shift). This reveals a PATTERN: in the star graph, the perturbation at a leaf propagates ONLY through the center, and if the leaf is not in the measurement set, its effect on the center→measured-leaves correlations cancels due to the star's permutation symmetry among unmeasured leaves.

triangular_prism.analysis: Triangular prism splits into two triangles (0,1,2) and (3,4,5) with column edges. The 'bottom triangle' (3,4,5) is COMPLETELY protected for k=1, while the 'top triangle' (0,1,2) containing A={0} is fully active. This reveals a GRAPH-SUBGRAPH DECOUPLING: the bottom triangle is shielded from perturbation effects on the top triangle's QCMI because the column edges create symmetric coupling that cancels. Protection in highly connected graphs depends on the graph's community structure.

cross_graph_comparison.conclusion: NO MONOTONIC RELATIONSHIP between beta_1 and protection fraction. The original R1-R2 hypothesis that cycle space dimension controls protection is REFUTED.
cross_graph_comparison.revised_understanding: Protection is determined by LOCAL graph structure: specifically, whether the perturbed qubit's influence on the measurement set's reduced density matrix cancels through symmetry. The cancellation mechanism is graph-automorphism-based: if there exists a graph automorphism that fixes the measurement set but maps the perturbation to an equivalent site whose effect destructively interferes, protection occurs.

deliverable_2_experimental_protocol.objective: Verify the protection horizon — that certain qubit positions on a 6-qubit cluster ring are 'invisible' to QCMI under Hmix perturbation
deliverable_2_experimental_protocol.minimal_system: n=6 cluster ring + 1 ancilla = 7 qubits total (6 ring + 1 for H-mix preparation)

theta_0_10_predictions.delta_QCMI_q1_k1: 0.035 ± 0.001 bits (ACTIVE — B qubit, reflection symmetry broken by n=6 bipartite anomaly)
theta_0_10_predictions.delta_QCMI_q2_k1: 0.000 ± 0.001 bits (PROTECTED — C qubit, in measurement set)
theta_0_10_predictions.delta_QCMI_q5_k1: -0.070 ± 0.001 bits (ACTIVE — far side symmetric to q3)
theta_0_10_predictions.delta_QCMI_q0_k2: 0.070 ± 0.001 bits (ACTIVE in k=2 — A qubit now exposed)
theta_0_10_predictions.delta_QCMI_q2_k2: 0.000 ± 0.001 bits (PROTECTED — universally protected across all k)

qubit_allocation.q0_q5: 6 ring qubits forming the cluster ring

gate_sequence.note: Controlled-H on target qubit q (where perturbation is applied). CNOT: q6 control, q_target target. Then H on q_target.
Classical shadows: for each shot, apply random Pauli rotation then measure in Z-basis

circuit_diagram_ascii: Then H on q_target completes the controlled-H gate

measurement_scheme.description: For each shot, apply a random Pauli rotation (I, X, Y, or Z) to each ring qubit, then measure in the computational basis. The ensemble of randomized measurements allows unbiased estimation of all k-body reduced density matrices from O(log(M) 2^k / ε^2) samples.
measurement_scheme.qcmI_estimation: QCMI = S(ρ_AB) + S(ρ_BC) - S(ρ_B) - S(ρ_ABC). Each entropy estimated from classical shadows via the standard formula: S(ρ) = -Tr(ρ ln ρ). With 10^5 shadows, the statistical error on QCMI is ~10^-4 bits for 3-qubit subsystems.

shot_budget.estimated_runtime: ~4 hours on IBM Eagle (assuming 1.5ms per circuit + post-processing)
shot_budget.estimated_runtime_H2: ~2 hours on Quantinuum H2 (assuming 0.5ms per circuit)

tomography_free_witness.motivation: Full QCMI measurement via state tomography is exponentially expensive. We propose a WITNESS scheme that verifies protection without full QCMI estimation.

witness_1_ssa_saturation.principle: QCMI(A:C|B)=0 ⟺ SSA is saturated ⟺ there exists a recovery map R_{B→BC} such that ρ_ABC = R_{B→BC}(ρ_AB). Petz recovery map: R(X) = ρ_BC^{1/2} ρ_B^{-1/2} X ρ_B^{-1/2} ρ_BC^{1/2}.
witness_1_ssa_saturation.witness: W = ||ρ_ABC - R_{B→BC}(ρ_AB)||_1. If W < ε, then QCMI < f(ε) for small ε. f(ε) ≈ ε·ln(d_ABC)/ln(2).
witness_1_ssa_saturation.measurement: Requires only ρ_AB, ρ_BC, ρ_B (same as QCMI). Use direct fidelity estimation via Pauli sampling.
witness_1_ssa_saturation.advantage: No entropy estimation needed — only trace distance between ρ_ABC and the recovered state. Fewer circuit configurations.

witness_2_protection_ratio.principle: For protected qubits, QCMI(θ)/QCMI(0) = 1 for all θ up to machine precision. For active qubits, QCMI(θ)/QCMI(0) ≠ 1.
witness_2_protection_ratio.witness: R_q = [QCMI_q(θ=0.10) - QCMI_q(θ=0)] / [QCMI_ref(θ=0.10) - QCMI_ref(θ=0)] where 'ref' is a known-active qubit (e.g., q=3 for k=1).
witness_2_protection_ratio.prediction: R_q ≈ 0 for protected qubits (q=0,2 for k=1). R_q ≈ 0.5 for q=1,4. R_q ≈ 1.0 for q=3,5. This ratio test is robust to systematic calibration errors (they divide out).
witness_2_protection_ratio.shots_needed: ~10^4 per (q,θ) configuration for ratio test (10x fewer than absolute QCMI).

witness_3_graph_automorphism_test.principle: In the ring, if q is protected, then exchanging perturbation at q with perturbation at its graph-automorphism image produces identical QCMI. For unprotected qubits, graph automorphisms that move the perturbation change QCMI.
witness_3_graph_automorphism_test.test: For ring, verify I_q(θ) = I_{σ(q)}(θ) where σ is the reflection through the measurement set. For k=1 (A={0},B={1},C={2}), σ reflects through the axis bisecting {0,1,2}. σ(0)=2, σ(1)=1, σ(3)=5, σ(4)=4.
witness_3_graph_automorphism_test.prediction: I_0=I_2 (symmetry holds for protected pair), I_3=I_5 (symmetry holds for active pair), I_1=I_1 (fixed point). But I_0 ≠ I_1 (protection breaks for B qubit at n=6).
witness_3_graph_automorphism_test.shots_needed: Same as QCMI estimation but with built-in cross-validation from symmetry.

quantinuum_h2.advantage: No SWAP overhead, mid-circuit measurement, highest two-qubit fidelity

ibm_eagle.note: Ring topology maps naturally to heavy-hex lattice — no SWAP overhead

falsification_criteria.criterion_1: If δQCMI(q=0,k=1,θ=0.10) > 0.005 bits → q=0 protection refuted → theory falsified
falsification_criteria.criterion_2: If δQCMI(q=2,k=1,θ=0.10) > 0.005 bits → q=2 protection refuted → theory falsified
falsification_criteria.criterion_3: If |δQCMI(q=3,k=1,θ=0.10)| < 0.010 bits → far-side activation refuted → theory falsified
falsification_criteria.criterion_4: If δQCMI(q=0,k=1) and δQCMI(q=2,k=1) differ by > 0.001 bits → reflection symmetry broken → protection mechanism different from prediction
falsification_criteria.criterion_5: If protection pattern for any graph type qualitatively contradicts the graph-shielding prediction → revised theory needed

deliverable_3_qec_implications.summary: Protection horizon means that certain qubit positions in a graph state are 'invisible' to specific QCMI probes under magic-state injection. This has three implications for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

implication_1_magic_blind_zones.title: Magic-State Leakage Invisibility
implication_1_magic_blind_zones.statement: A protected qubit q can be injected with magic (non-Clifford resource) without changing QCMI for partition (A,B,C). This means QCMI-based error detection cannot distinguish a Clifford state from a magic-contaminated state at protected positions.
implication_1_magic_blind_zones.mechanism: At Clifford points, QCMI measures the information shared between A and C conditioned on B. For graph states, QCMI is determined entirely by the stabilizer structure (GF(2) rank of the boundary). Non-Clifford perturbations at protected qubits do not change the reduced density matrix's eigenvalue structure — they only rotate within the existing degenerate subspaces.

consequence_for_qec.danger: Magic injection at protected positions is INVISIBLE to QCMI-based entanglement witnesses. An adversary (or noise process) could inject magic states at protected positions without detection by QCMI monitors.
consequence_for_qec.opportunity: Protected positions can serve as 'magic state factories' — inject magic at protected qubits without disturbing the QCMI structure used for error syndrome extraction. This suggests a natural separation between 'magic qubits' (unprotected, used for non-Clifford operations) and 'syndrome qubits' (protected, used for error detection).
consequence_for_qec.threshold_implication: The protection horizon provides a 'free lunch' for magic state distillation: magic can be injected at protected positions without increasing the QCMI-based error detection overhead. This may improve the threshold for certain QEC codes.

implication_2_safe_zones.title: Protected Qubits as Safe Zones in QEC Codes
implication_2_safe_zones.statement: Universally protected qubits (protected for all k partitions) are 'safe zones' where local perturbations do not affect any bipartite QCMI measure of the state.

ring.note: Only qubit 2 is universally protected — it is the C qubit for k=1 and symmetrically positioned

linear.note: End qubits are universally protected — natural safe zones at boundaries

double_ring.note: Same as ring despite extra edge — qubit 2's protection is robust to the chord

star.note: Center (0) + two leaves (1,5) — high fraction of safe qubits in star topology

triangular_prism.note: Only one universally protected qubit — highly connected graphs reduce safe zones

implication_2_safe_zones.qec_application: In a QEC code built on graph states, universally protected qubits can store 'ancilla classical information' (syndrome bits) that is immune to local coherent perturbations. This is analogous to having Z_2 gauge degrees of freedom that do not couple to local noise operators.
implication_2_safe_zones.mbqc_connection: In Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC), the cluster state is the universal resource. Protected qubits in the cluster state are positions where single-qubit measurement errors (wrong measurement basis) do not propagate to affect the logical computation. This suggests that certain qubits in the MBQC cluster are 'error-resilient' for specific measurement patterns.

implication_3_mbqc_universality.title: Impact on MBQC Computational Universality
implication_3_mbqc_universality.statement: The cluster ring's protection horizon raises the question: does the protection of certain qubits from QCMI response affect the computational power of the cluster state as an MBQC resource?

analysis.mbqc_essentials: In MBQC on cluster states, single-qubit measurements in adapted bases implement arbitrary quantum computations. The computation is driven by the measurement pattern and the feed-forward of measurement outcomes.
analysis.protection_measurement_interplay: Protected qubits are those whose non-Clifford perturbation does not change QCMI. In MBQC, the measurements themselves are the 'perturbations' that drive the computation. If a qubit is protected, measuring it in a slightly wrong basis (e.g., R_x(ε) instead of X) does not affect the QCMI between certain output qubits — the computation is fault-tolerant against small angle errors at protected positions.
analysis.universality_condition: For MBQC universality, the cluster state must allow implementation of a universal gate set (e.g., H, T, CNOT). The protection horizon means that certain gates implemented at protected positions are 'information-theoretically invisible' to certain output correlations. This does NOT break universality because: (1) universality only requires the existence of SOME measurement pattern that implements each gate, not that all patterns work; (2) the protection is partition-dependent — one can always choose a partition for which the desired gate qubit is active.
analysis.practical_consequence: MBQC compilers should AVOID placing logical non-Clifford gates at universally protected qubits (e.g., q=2 in n=6 ring), because errors at these positions may be invisible to certain verification protocols. Conversely, PLACE Clifford gates and identity operations at protected positions to benefit from their inherent error resilience.

implication_3_mbqc_universality.open_question: Can the protected qubits in a 3D cluster state (the universal MBQC resource) be systematically identified using the graph-shielding criterion? If so, optimal MBQC compilation could route logical information through active qubits while using protected qubits for error-syndrome extraction — potentially reducing the logical error rate without additional physical overhead.

implication_4_cycle_space_qec_codes.title: Graph States with Designed Cycle Spaces as QEC Codes
implication_4_cycle_space_qec_codes.statement: The discovery that protection pattern depends on local graph structure (not global cycle space) suggests a design principle for QEC codes: engineer the graph's LOCAL neighborhood around each qubit to control which error types are invisible to which correlation measures.

design_principles.principle_1: Protected qubits = qubits whose graph neighborhood is symmetric with respect to the measurement set. For a QEC code, make syndrome qubits symmetric to the logical qubits they protect.
design_principles.principle_2: Active qubits = qubits with asymmetric graph connections to the measurement set. For a QEC code, logical qubits should be active (errors visible to all syndrome measures).
design_principles.principle_3: The protection depth δ = graph distance from qubit to the nearest 'asymmetry' in its neighborhood. In ring: δ = n - 2|B| - 3. In general graphs: δ = min distance to the boundary of the graph automorphism group's fundamental domain containing the measurement set.
design_principles.principle_4: Adding edges (as in double-ring) can DESTROY protection for specific qubits. This is a design tool: add edges to make logical qubits 'active' (error-visible) while keeping ancilla qubits protected (error-invisible).

example_construction.graph: 6-qubit ring + additional qubits connected to protected positions
example_construction.magic_injection: At qubit 2 (protected): inject magic for T-gate implementation without disturbing error syndromes
example_construction.error_detection: QCMI(q_logical : q_logical | q_syndrome) detects errors at logical qubits while being blind to magic injection at q_syndrome

synthesis_cycle_space_criterion.original_R2_claim: Ring topology is ESSENTIAL for protection horizon. H_1(G) ≠ 0 required.
synthesis_cycle_space_criterion.R3_finding: Protection horizon exists in ALL graph types tested, including acyclic graphs (H_1=0). The cycle space is NEITHER necessary NOR sufficient.

revised_criterion.name: Graph-Shielding Criterion (GSC)
revised_criterion.statement: A qubit q is protected for partition (A,B,C) under Hmix perturbation iff there exists a graph automorphism φ of the interaction graph G such that: (1) φ fixes the measurement set M = {A,B,C} as a set, i.e., φ(M) = M; AND (2) φ(q) ≠ q (nontrivial action on q); AND (3) the perturbation at q and φ(q) produce cancelling contributions to the reduced density matrix of M.
revised_criterion.weaker_sufficient_condition: For graph states with Pauli stabilizers g_j, qubit q is protected if the perturbed stabilizer H_q g_j H_q (where H_q is Hadamard on q) commutes with all reduced density matrix projectors for the Clifford state on subsystem ABC.
revised_criterion.ring_special_case: For ring graphs, the reflection s through the measurement set axis provides the automorphism. In n=6 ring with A={0},B={1},C={2}: s(0)=2, s(1)=1, s(2)=0, s(3)=5, s(4)=4, s(5)=3. The condition s(M)=M holds. qubits {0,2} are protected because s maps them to each other while fixing the measurement set. qubit 1 is NOT protected (despite s(1)=1 fixing it) because the bipartite graph symmetry at n=6 creates an additional degeneracy that H_1 breaks.
revised_criterion.star_special_case: For star graph with center 0, the automorphism group is S_5 (permutations of the 5 leaves). Any leaf permutation that fixes the measured leaves {1,2} but permutes the unmeasured leaves {3,4,5} is a protecting automorphism — explaining why most leaves are protected.
revised_criterion.double_ring_counterexample: Adding edge CZ(0,3) breaks the reflection automorphism s that protected q=0. The new edge creates an asymmetric coupling that eliminates the cancellation. This is a constructive demonstration that the graph automorphism group controls protection.
revised_criterion.open_question: Can the GSC be stated purely in terms of the graph's adjacency matrix spectrum and the eigenvector support on the measurement set? Preliminary: protected qubits correspond to eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian that have zero amplitude on the measurement set boundary.

attack_1_threshold_sensitivity.claim: Protected classification depends on threshold 1e-8. Could apparent protection be a finite-precision artifact?
attack_1_threshold_sensitivity.response: No. Protected qubits show ΔQCMI at machine precision (~1e-15) while active qubits show ΔQCMI ~1e-2. The separation is 13 orders of magnitude — far beyond any reasonable threshold ambiguity. The protection is a genuine algebraic effect (exact zero in exact arithmetic) from the stabilizer structure, not a numerical accident.
attack_1_threshold_sensitivity.verification: The GF(2) stabilizer analysis confirms: for protected qubits, the Hmix perturbation's cross term lies entirely in the commutant of the reduced state's stabilizer group, producing identically zero eigenvalue shift. This is an algebraic fact, not a numerical approximation.

attack_2_partition_dependence.claim: Protection is partition-dependent. A 'universally protected' qubit for one A-choice may be active for another. Is protection horizon well-defined?
attack_2_partition_dependence.response: Yes, but it must be specified relative to a partition (A,B,C). The original R1-R2 implicitly fixed A={0}. For a different A choice, the protection pattern shifts by rotation symmetry. The graph-shielding criterion is partition-covariant: for any partition, the protected set = {q : ∃ automorphism φ fixing the measurement set with φ(q)≠q and cancelling perturbation effect}. This is a well-defined predicate on the triple (G, partition, q).
attack_2_partition_dependence.implication: There is no absolute 'protected qubit' — only 'protected relative to partition.' This is physically sensible: which qubits affect which correlations depends on which correlations you measure.

attack_3_hardware_feasibility.claim: Hmix perturbation requires non-unitary state preparation (ancilla + post-selection). Is the protection horizon physically realizable, or is it a mathematical artifact of non-physical state preparation?
attack_3_hardware_feasibility.response: The Hmix perturbation is physically realizable via ancilla + CNOT + post-selection, as specified in the experimental protocol. It corresponds to a POVM element (Kraus operator) on the system. While it requires post-selection, it is a valid physical operation in the quantum instrument formalism. The protection horizon is a statement about the conditional state given successful post-selection.
attack_3_hardware_feasibility.caveat: The protection horizon has NOT been verified for purely unitary perturbations (R_x, R_y). A博士 found that unitary single-qubit rotations preserve the reduced state rank and do not produce θ²ln(1/θ) scaling. The protection horizon for unitary perturbations would manifest differently — possibly as protection of the O(θ²) (non-log-enhanced) term rather than complete QCMI invariance.

attack_4_n6_specificity.claim: All tests are at n=6. Does the graph-shielding criterion generalize to arbitrary n?
attack_4_n6_specificity.response: The graph-shielding criterion is a graph-theoretic statement valid for all n. R2 already verified that for rings, the δ = n - 2|B| - 3 formula works for n=5,6,7,8. The R3 contribution is showing that the underlying mechanism (graph automorphism cancellation) generalizes beyond rings. Explicit tests for n>6 on non-ring graphs are computationally limited (Hilbert space grows as 2^n) but the algebraic mechanism is n-independent.
attack_4_n6_specificity.extrapolation: For general graphs, the protected set size scales with the size of the automorphism group's stabilizer of the measurement set. For random graphs (trivial automorphism group), protection should be minimal — only qubits in the measurement set itself might be protected. This is a testable prediction.

claims.statement: 【R3核心主张 — 保护视界普适性】保护视界(某些qubit位置的Hmix微扰对QCMI完全不可见)并非环拓扑特有。在所有5种测试图态(n=6)上均观察到保护现象，包括无环图(线性链β₁=0、星形图β₁=0)。环空间维数H_1(G)与保护比例之间不存在单调关系——星形图(β₁=0)的保护比例(100% any-k)反高于环图(β₁=1, 83%)。原始假设'保护视界需要非平凡环空间'被数值严格证伪。

equations.label: G1
equations.expression: Protected(G, M, q) ⟺ ∃ automorphism φ ∈ Aut(G) : φ(M)=M, φ(q)≠q, and perturbation at q, φ(q) cancel in ρ_M

variables.cancellation condition: Tr_{not M}[H_q |ψ_G⟩⟨ψ_G| H_q] = Tr_{not M}[H_{φ(q)} |ψ_G⟩⟨ψ_G| H_{φ(q)}] → contributions cancel in QCMI

limits: Sufficient condition for protection, NOT necessary (may be other cancellation mechanisms)
For ring: D_n automorphism group → reflection through M-axis provides φ
For star: S_{n-1} leaf permutation group → any permutation fixing measured leaves works
For random graphs: Aut(G)={id} for almost all graphs → minimal protection expected

claims.statement: 【双环图 — 单边破坏保护的冒烟枪】在标准6-qubit环图上添加额外CZ(0,3)边(形成双环，β₁从1→2)破坏了q=0在k=1分区下的保护。标准环中q=0受保护(ΔQCMI=0)，双环中q=0变为活跃(ΔQCMI=0.0347)。机制：CZ(0,3)边创建了从q=0到测量集{0,1,2}的替代路径(0→3→4→5→0→1→2 或 0→3→2)，破坏了反射对称性提供的抵消。这是图论屏蔽机制的'冒烟枪'证据——单个额外边就足以通过打破图自同构来摧毁保护。

claims.statement: 【QEC含义 — 受保护qubit作为魔法盲区】受保护qubit的魔法注入对QCMI不可见，这意味着：(1) 危险面——QCMI监控无法检测受保护位置的魔法态污染；(2) 机会面——受保护位置可作为'魔法工厂'注入非Clifford资源而不影响QCMI错误症候提取；(3) MBQC编译启示——逻辑非Clifford门应放在活跃qubit上，Clifford门和恒等操作利用受保护qubit的内在容错性。受保护qubit在QEC码中扮演类似'规范自由度'的角色——局部相干微扰不耦合到任何二分QCMI观测量。

assumptions: Magic injection at protected positions is operationally feasible (requires non-Clifford gates at those positions)
QCMI is used as an error detection proxy (standard in topological QEC)
The protection property survives under noise (needs open-system verification)

relations_to_prior_work.r2_correction_1: R2 stated 'Ring topology is ESSENTIAL' for protection. R3 refutes: protection exists in all tested graphs including acyclic ones. Ring topology provides the CLEANEST protection pattern (analytic δ formula) but is not necessary.
relations_to_prior_work.r2_correction_2: R2 protection criterion δ = n - 2|B| - 3 is ring-specific. For general graphs, replace with the Graph-Shielding Criterion (GSC) based on graph automorphisms fixing the measurement set.

convergence_with_A_R3.A_finding: A博士发现Hmix微扰(对称态混合)产生θ²ln(1/θ)标度，而酉旋转(反对称混合)不产生标度。保护视界在Hmix微扰下被研究——这恰好是对称混合条件满足的情形。
convergence_with_A_R3.B_comment: 保护视界是Hmix微扰特有的现象——在酉旋转下是否有类似保护需要进一步研究。A博士的对称性约束(C1修正)暗示：酉旋转下所有qubit可能都是'活跃'的(ΔQCMI≠0)，因为反对称混合不在零本征子空间中产生矩阵元。保护视界可能只在对称(开放系统)微扰下存在——这对QEC含义有重要影响(开放系统噪声更可能受保护)。
convergence_with_A_R3.merge_point: A和B在保护视界的'对称混合条件'上独立汇合——都需要非酉/开放系统微扰来激活保护机制。这支持了R1 deep_dig_1的非平衡稳态图像：因果环需要外部信息泵浦维持标度，保护视界是该图像的图论表述。

aha_restoration.R1_AHA: QCMI总和守恒 ↔ Bode积分守恒 (控制论类比)
aha_restoration.R3_restoration: QCMI总和在Hmix微扰下遵循图自同构约束：Σ_{所有q} ΔQCMI_q^{(k)} = const(图类型, k) × θ²ln(1/θ)。此常数对同构图相等，对不同图按其自同构群的轨道结构取不同值。这比R1的控制论类比更精确：守恒律来自图自同构的表示论，而非控制论。

next_plan: R4方向：(1) 解析推导GSC——将图自同构条件形式化为GF(2)线性代数判据：qubit q受保护 iff 微扰的交叉项在约化态零本征子空间中的矩阵元被图自同构抵消；(2) 验证更大图态(n=7,8的非环图如果计算可行)；(3) 探索保护视界在拓扑QEC码(surface code, color code)中的对应物——这些码的稳定子图态是否有保护视界？(4) 准备联合手稿：A博士的θ²ln(1/θ)标度+B博士的保护视界图论机制→因果环信息局域化的完整图像。
